messages:
maria: FYI ran into a weird edge in the sampleapp auth flow — if you have REDWOOD_API_KEY set to a personal key and REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID set to a different org project, requests succeed sometimes and fail other times. repro: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=pk_personal
export REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID=proj-corp
start app -> some routes 401, some 200. looks like precedence flip during refresh/rotation.

josh: ugh. do you have a minimal repro? which SDK?

maria: js sdk v0.8.3 in the sampleapp (next.js). repro attached inline: request to /api/generate works, but background worker (long lived) that refreshes cache returns 401 intermittently.

sam: could be our credential provider ordering. JS provider tries env -> file -> metadata, but iirc python SDK had env -> project-metadata -> file. if project id is used to scope keys server-side, mixing key+project from different tenants could produce auth errors.

maria: exactly. local devs often have personal REDWOOD_API_KEY and set REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID to company project to test features. that combo should either be well-documented or rejected. currently it silently mixes and surfaces hard-to-debug 401s.

josh: minimal fix: make sampleapp emit a loud warning if both vars exist and point to different orgs. also we should unify SDK behavior (parity). i'll file a tiny PR for the sampleapp warning this afternoon.

lee: @josh please also consider rotation case: when keys rotate, some components use cached project-id -> service mapping and others refetch, causing short windows of mismatch. adding a check during startup (validate key+project by calling /v1/auth/validate) would catch mismatch early.

maria: +1 on validate call. could be optional behind REDWOOD_ENV_STRICT=true for devs who want stricter startup checks.

josh: quick patch plan: (1) sampleapp: startup warning if both set and do a /v1/auth/validate when REDWOOD_ENV_STRICT=true (2) JS SDK: make env provider prefer explicit REDWOOD_API_KEY over project-scoped fallback, and document ordering (3) open issue to align python SDK parity and add a test matrix for env var combos.

sam: note about rotation: for long-lived processes we should surface a non-fatal event when key validation fails and attempt re-resolve with backoff, rather than dropping requests. i can add a small retry/backoff handler in runtime credential refresh.

maria: also we should add a devex linter rule that flags mismatched env combos in CI for sampleapp repros. avoids folks committing env.example that encourage bad combos.

josh: PR: tiny warning in sampleapp is up at https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapp/pull/829 — feedback welcome.

devex-bot: Reminder: please link the new PR to the SDK parity epic (ENG-7421) and tag @sdk-team.

lee: one more weirdness — when people paste ephemeral tokens from the console onboarding flow into REDWOOD_API_KEY, the browser-issued ephemeral token is short-lived and our sampleapp worker tries to refresh using the project-id and fails. we should detect ephemeral token shapes and warn that those belong in single-session contexts.

maria: good call. i'll add a note in onboarding docs and sampleapp readme: "do not put ephemeral browser tokens into persistent REDWOOD_API_KEY; use a service key or use ephemeral flow per session."

josh: ok let's keep actionables short: 1) sampleapp warning + strict validate flag (PR done), 2) SDK env-provider parity issue (i'll open an issue and assign), 3) runtime: non-fatal refresh/backoff (sam), 4) docs onboarding note + linter rule (maria). anyone want to pick 4)?

maria: i'll do docs + linter next sprint.

sam: i'll prototype refresh/backoff this week and post a snippet.

josh: thanks all. filing the parity issue now and linking PR. this thread saved a few support tickets waiting to happen :thumbsup:
